topbar.sessionTitle: Session status, frame, modules and settings
topbar.focusTitle: Emacs gets the whole window: the lesson and the side panels step aside. Where the browser allows, it also goes fullscreen and locks the keyboard so Ctrl+W and friends reach Emacs. Leave with this button or Shift+Esc.

frame.label: Frame
frame.guiTitle: Graphical frame: the same Emacs, with the same buffers, drawn with images and mouse menus (PDFs, images). Switch back to the terminal at any time.
frame.terminalTitle: Terminal frame: Emacs in a terminal, crisp text and every key
frame.guiUnavailable: The GUI frame is not enabled on this server
frame.starting: Graphical frame: the same Emacs drawn with images and mouse menus. Starting…
frame.guiTimeout: The GUI frame did not start. The terminal frame keeps working; try again from the session page.

screen.terminalLabel: Emacs, terminal frame. Shift+Escape moves focus to the lesson.
screen.headerGui: Emacs {{version}}, GUI frame on Xvnc via noVNC
screen.modulesTitle: Configuration modules loaded in this Emacs

overlay.startingBody: The playground is starting a session. The first start takes a few seconds.
overlay.replaced: This Emacs is open somewhere else.
overlay.replacedBody: Another tab or window attached to the terminal. Your work is safe; take it back here whenever you like.
overlay.restartingBody: Your files are safe, and your keys wait. Buffers come back from the last snapshot in a moment.
overlay.frameClosedBody: C-x C-c ran save-buffers-kill-terminal. The playground is reopening your frame; buffers are intact because Emacs runs as a daemon. On your own machine this would quit Emacs.
overlay.suspendedBody: C-z sent Emacs to the background of the shell. Resuming it for you. (In a real terminal you would type fg.)
overlay.stoppingBody: Your workspace is kept. Reload the page to start it again.
overlay.unavailableBody: Retrying. If this lasts, use Restart Emacs on the session page.
overlay.modulesBody: Emacs restarts with the modules this part teaches and the lesson is set up again. Your buffers come back; your keys wait until then.
overlay.busyBody: It has not answered for a few seconds.

ticker.label: Key ticker: the keys you pressed and the commands they ran
ticker.empty: Press a key in the Emacs pane. Every chord shows up here with the command it ran.
ticker.prefixGloss: This is a prefix: it does nothing alone.
ticker.gap: Some keys were missed while reconnecting.

where.waiting: Waiting for Emacs to report its state…
where.calm: Nothing unusual is going on. You are editing normally.

nudges.empty: Nothing to translate yet. VS Code habits that do something else in Emacs will show up here, once each.

rescue.explain: Cancels any prompt, closes extra windows, widens, stops macros and overwrite mode. Never touches your files.
rescue.resetExplain: Puts the files and windows back to how this step started; changes since then are lost.
rescue.resetTitle: Restore the files and layout for this step from its checkpoint
rescue.resetConfirmBody: The files and windows go back to how this step started. Changes you made since then are lost.
rescue.nothing: Rescue: you were already in a normal state. Nothing changed.
rescue.noStep: No step is active, so there is nothing to reset.
rescue.restored_one: Restored {{count}} file and the Emacs layout from this step's checkpoint.
rescue.restored_other: Restored {{count}} files and the Emacs layout from this step's checkpoint.
rescue.restoredShort: files and layout restored from the step checkpoint
rescue.restored_zero: Restored the Emacs layout from this step's checkpoint; no files had changed.

stuck.button: I'm stuck: tell the course author
stuck.title: Report that you are stuck
stuck.explain: This sends your last few hundred keys and what Emacs showed to the people who maintain the course, so the lesson can be improved. Your files are not sent.
stuck.noteLabel: What were you trying to do? (optional)
stuck.sentBody: Thanks, the report was sent. If you would rather move on, Emacs can do this step for you.
stuck.skipping: Emacs is doing this step for you…
stuck.skippingBody: Watch the screen: the keys are played for you. Your own keys wait until it is done.

lesson.loadFailed: Could not load the lesson files into Emacs: {{error}}
lesson.notFound: This lesson is not written yet.
lesson.notFoundBody: It is on the course map as planned. Pick another lesson for now.
lesson.noSuchLesson: There is no lesson at this address.
lesson.noSuchLessonBody: The link may be mistyped or out of date. Every lesson is on the course map.
lesson.displaced: Emacs is now showing another lesson, opened in another tab or window. This lesson's steps are not being checked.

steps.label: Steps
steps.noHint: No hint for this one: try "Watch it".
steps.jumpingBody: Emacs is setting up the lesson as the earlier steps leave it. Your own keys wait until it is done.

demo.watchTitle: Watch Emacs do this step slowly, every key named below the screen. Watching does not count as done: you do it yourself afterwards. Press any key to stop.
demo.fromStart: Starting from the beginning of this step.
demo.waitingFirst: the first key comes in a moment
demo.watched: You watched this step. Now do it yourself.
demo.doItTitle: Put the files and windows back to how this step started, then do it with your own keys
demo.notActive: This step is not the current one any more; the demo was not played.
demo.cancelled: Demo stopped: you pressed a key.
demo.bad: This step's demo cannot be played: {{error}}

terminal.reservedKey: Your browser may keep that key for itself (Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+N…). Focus mode, top right, locks the keyboard so the keys reach Emacs.

focus.banner: Focus mode: keys go to Emacs, and the lesson and panels step aside.
focus.trying: Asking the browser for fullscreen and the keyboard…
focus.lockOn: The keyboard is locked: Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+N reach Emacs too.
focus.lockOff: This browser keeps Ctrl+W, Ctrl+T and Ctrl+N; Chrome and Edge lock them in fullscreen.

startOver.title: Start over?
startOver.body: This clears the progress of every lesson: ticks, hints and resets. Your files and Emacs stay as they are.
startOver.done: Progress cleared: every lesson starts fresh.

preview.empty: Nothing to preview yet. Use the ◧ button next to a file in the tree.
preview.missingFollow: It is built from {{source}}: save that file, or run the build the task describes. The preview appears as soon as the file does.
preview.missingBody: It appears here as soon as the file is written.

checkpoints.none: No checkpoints yet. One is taken when each task starts.
checkpoints.willOverwrite_one: This overwrites {{count}} file with the version from the checkpoint:
checkpoints.willOverwrite_other: This overwrites {{count}} files with the version from the checkpoint:
checkpoints.nothingChanged: No files differ from this checkpoint; the Emacs layout is restored.
checkpoints.keeps: Build folders (target, _build, .venv) are kept. Your Git staging area is reset to the checkpoint.

project.complete: Project complete. Every task is done.
project.notFound: This project is not written yet.
project.notFoundBody: It is listed on the course map as planned.
project.noSuchProject: There is no project at this address.
project.noSuchProjectBody: The link may be mistyped or out of date. Every project is on the course map.
project.lapIntro: Do every task once more from the start, with hints and demos turned off and a timer running, to see what stuck. Your files go back to how the project started.
project.lapStartTitle: Restores the project's files and starts at task 1 without hints
project.lapRunning: Lap without hints: hints, demos and skipping are off until the last task is done.
project.lapStopTitle: Hints come back; this task starts again from its checkpoint
project.lapOverTarget: The target is {{time}}; another lap will be quicker.

course.title: From the first keystroke to your own config
course.intro: Fifteen parts, each unlocking a piece of a real development setup. Every lesson runs inside the same pre-configured Emacs you take home at the end. The order is a suggestion: start anywhere.
course.finishedTitle: Every step is done, watched or skipped. Open the lesson to practise the steps you watched or skipped.
course.projectsBelow: See the project list below. Each project has its own checkpoints.
course.projectsIntro: Each project mirrors something you already do in VS Code, task by task, with checkpoints you can return to. Later projects mix languages on purpose.

session.title: Your session
session.ledeLocal: One Emacs runs in a container on this machine. Your files live in ./workspace next to compose.yaml.
session.ledeServer: Your Emacs runs in a container on the server. Your files are kept between visits.
session.restartBody: The last resort when Emacs is stuck. Files are safe; unsaved edits since the last auto-save (5 s) may be lost. Buffers are reopened from the last snapshot.
session.stopBody: The container stops; your workspace and progress are kept. Opening a lesson starts it again.
session.progressBody: Your ticks, hints and resets for every lesson. Starting over clears them; your files, checkpoints and Emacs configuration stay.
session.frameBody: The same Emacs can show a terminal frame (crisp text, every key) or a GUI frame (PDFs and images). Buffers are shared; switching is instant.
session.modulesBody: Parts of the course unlock modules of the Emacs configuration as they teach them. You can turn them on early here; Emacs restarts with your buffers.
session.modulesRestarting: Emacs is restarting with the new modules.
session.byoBody: The same Emacs can be attached from a native terminal (kitty, WezTerm, iTerm2), with the full keyboard. The browser keeps showing the lesson and the ticker.
session.byoServer: On a server, only the browser can attach to your Emacs.
session.exportLocal: Everything you build, including your growing Emacs configuration in emacs.d, is in ./workspace. Copy it to keep it:
session.exportServer: Ask the operator for an export of your workspace (playctl export-user). A download button is planned.
session.screenReader: Screen reader mode for the terminal

login.title: Sign in
login.heading: Welcome to Emacs Playground
login.lede: Enter the invite code you were given to start your own Emacs.
login.badCode: That code was not accepted. Check it and try again.

emacs.restarted: Emacs restarted; your files are safe.
emacs.modulesLoaded: Loaded the configuration modules for this part of the course.

notices.guiNeeded: This lesson uses the GUI frame: the same Emacs drawn as a graphical window, with images, PDFs and mouse menus. It opens on its own; you went back to the terminal.
notices.guiOn: You are in the GUI frame: the same Emacs and buffers, drawn as a graphical window. Click it before typing. The Terminal half of the switch above the screen brings the terminal back.
notices.guiOff: This lesson needs the GUI frame, which this server has turned off. Read along; the steps that need images cannot be done here.
notices.boxReady: SSH box ready: /ssh:box: opens its files from any prompt.
notices.boxNotReady: The SSH box is still being set up. The steps that use /ssh:box: work once it is ready.
notices.boxUnknown: This lesson uses the SSH box: /ssh:box: opens its files from any prompt.
notices.boxOff: This lesson uses an SSH box, which this server does not provide. Read along; the remote steps cannot be done here.
